Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates are passed: the excess is greater than 0.80 km in absolute terms AND greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km (14.44), not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km (14.4), which POL-RD-01 expressly forbids citing for the threshold test.

The excess rests on an unimpaired trace and needs no independent corroboration. The trace carries 114 fixes at a 10 s sampling interval with 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met: there is no gap over 90 s, no straight-line jump over 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 s. POL-RD-07(ii) therefore does not bite, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02818 and the same pickup and trip timestamps, and the excess is measured from an unimpaired trace. The rider also does not attract the extra corroboration requirement of POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the 4-claim trigger, so no second source beyond the trace is required.

The driver's explanation — 'Minor detour because of a road works sign' — cannot be tested and cannot exonerate him. With no advisory on file naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses, and no validity window, POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver cites no evidence ID for an advisory, POL-RD-13(1) governs: this is a gap in the bundle, not the invocation of an exculpatory clause against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire and the case does not escalate.

No rider instruction explains the excess. No relocation of the pickup or dropoff occurred: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so POL-RD-05 has no amended endpoints and no stored re-quote to apply. On the POL-RD-02 arithmetic the rider is owed a refund. fare_model on the fare_breakdown is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not apply. That refund is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so the outcome is not NO_ACTION, and it is 12.5% of charged_total, below the 90% share, so the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 2.60 and not a full refund. No separate pass-through correction is due, and nothing may be netted against the distance refund: the fare_breakdown carries no ERP gantry, no toll and no airport surcharge (erp_lines total SGD 0.00; airport_surcharge 0.00), and this trip does not originate at an airport. Every charged line — base fare 3.80, distance charge, time charge and the 0.80 platform fee — has a counterpart in the metered rate card and the trip record, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged and there is no unmatched line requiring escalation.

I do not press for a POL-RD-06 uplift and the record does not support one: this deviation is not MATERIAL (20.33% is below the 50% gate and 2.44 km is below the 8.0 km gate), and the driver_profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 1 over completed_trips_90d of 188 — below both the 3-flag threshold and the 0.05 ratio threshold. No repeat pattern is established, so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral follows, and no driver compensation arises either, the billed 14.4 km falling only 0.04 km short of the trace and far below the 1.0 km shortfall gate.

The present state of this payment is a full charge in place: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. NO_ACTION is party-relative and would leave the rider carrying the entire SGD 20.66 for a trip the trace shows ran 2.44 km and 20.33% over the optimal route. Only the POL-RD-02 refund, SGD 2.60, leaves the rider not carrying the charge attributable to the deviation.

Even taking the rider's case at its highest, the measured excess is 2.44 km — 20.33% over the 12.0 km optimal — which clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%) only narrowly, and is nowhere near the 8.0 km or the 50% figure that make a deviation MATERIAL. POL-RD-06 is therefore not engaged on this trip's own evidence, and nothing beyond the POL-RD-02 arithmetic is available to the rider on the record as it stands.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The driver's own trace (EV-GPS-02818) measures this trip at 14.44 km (gps_trace.trace_distance_km, the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing over the rounded 14.4 on the trip record) against the platform optimal of 12.00 km (EV-TRIP-02818) — an excess of 2.44 km, or 20.33% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass (over 0.80 km and over 20%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is NOT material (neither over 50% nor over 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not triggered: no FULL_REFUND uplift, and the driver profile (deviation_flags_90d = 1 over completed_trips_90d = 188, a 0.0053 ratio) establishes no repeat pattern in any event. The trace is clean for policy purposes — 114 fixes at 10 s, 100% coverage, no gaps, 0.0 s maximum gap — so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) does not fire, no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

Driver: your explanation of a road-works detour cannot be tested and exonerates nothing. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-02818-01, is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so there is no advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route uses and no validity window; POL-RD-03 is unavailable and under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 your assertion carries no weight. Because you cited no advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire and the case is decided on the record, not escalated.

No exclusions apply on any other ground: the chat log is empty (0 messages), so there is no POL-RD-04 rider instruction; pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, so POL-RD-05 has no amended endpoints; and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply.

Rider: the fare is recomputed under POL-RD-02 on the METERED fare. Stated on separate lines: charged_total = SGD 20.66; recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.28 x 16.0) x the 1.00 surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 18.08; refund = SGD 2.58, rounded up to SGD 2.60. There are no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge lines (the trip neither originates at an airport nor crosses a gantry), so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and no billing-integrity referral arises; no charged line is unmatched, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged. The refund is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 12.5% of charged_total, below the 90% share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

Driver: your argument that the exposure should be capped at the SGD 2.00 contested amount is rejected. The POL-RD-02 refund is arithmetic, not discretionary, and no clause caps it at the sum the rider put in issue; the platform's own money block enumerates SGD 2.60 as the payable figure.

No driver compensation is due: the billed distance (14.4 km) falls only 0.04 km short of the trace, far below the 1.0 km shortfall POL-RD-04 requires. The monetary effect (SGD 2.60) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically. Confidence 0.92, resting entirely on weight-1.0 artifacts. No clause produces a referral, and no escalation trigger fires.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
